learningObjective: Compute the arithmetic intensity of a batched matrix multiplication and compare it against a GPU's ridge point to determine bind regime.

canonicalClaims.claim: For a dense square GEMM M=N=K=n loaded once from HBM, arithmetic intensity is approximately n/3 FLOP/byte for FP16 operands (2·n^3 FLOPs / (3·n^2·2 B)), so AI scales with n and typical modern GPU ridge points place n ≥ ~few hundred squarely compute-bound.
conditions: All three matrices are streamed once from HBM and the tiled schedule realizes their intra-tile reuse.
AI is measured against HBM traffic rather than L1/SMEM traffic.
FP16 operands stored as 2 bytes each; accumulation precision does not affect HBM traffic.
nonImplications: Does not imply that any GEMM launch will reach the compute peak; occupancy, MMA scheduling and shared-memory bank behavior all affect achieved throughput.
Does not imply that GEMV (K=1024 but M=1) is compute-bound; GEMV has AI ≈ 1 FLOP/byte.

sourceMappings.locator: GEMM chapter, tile-level reuse and arithmetic intensity

misconceptions.claim: GEMM has the same arithmetic intensity as GEMV because both perform 2·N·K FLOPs per row of output.
misconceptions.whyWrong: GEMV amortizes weight loads over a single output vector (AI ≈ 1 FLOP/byte); GEMM amortizes them over N output columns, giving AI proportional to the tile K dimension.

misconceptions.claim: The Roofline classification depends on launch grid configuration.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The Roofline model classifies based on AI (algorithmic property) vs ridge point (hardware property); launch grid affects achieved efficiency toward that ceiling, not the ceiling itself.

misconceptions.claim: FP16 accumulation makes a GEMM memory-bound because accumulators spill.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Accumulation precision affects numeric behavior and Tensor Core selection, not the ratio of FLOPs to HBM bytes moved. Accumulator spills, if they occur, go to registers/local memory, and are unrelated to the AI vs ridge comparison.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: CUDA C++ Programming Guide, WMMA/MMA docs

misconceptions.claim: Modern GEMM kernels reach the ridge line automatically once AI > ridge point.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Being compute-bound in Roofline is necessary but not sufficient for peak throughput; scheduling, register/shared-memory pressure, and Tensor Core operand alignment all further gate achievable performance.

implementationFacts: GEMM FLOPs = 2·M·N·K; HBM bytes ≈ (M·K + K·N + M·N)·sizeof(dtype).
For M=N=K=n FP16, AI ≈ (2·n^3) / (3·n^2·2) = n/3 FLOP/byte.
A100 FP16 Tensor Core ridge ≈ 312 TFLOP/s ÷ 2 TB/s ≈ 156 FLOP/byte.
performanceScenarios: LLM training and prefill use large GEMMs with large K; they are typically compute-bound.
LLM decode uses GEMV (batch-1 linear); these are memory-bound and motivate weight quantization.
